dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Nam, how many siblings do you have? Just Fah?
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːm, ˈhaʊ ˈmɛni ˈsɪblɪŋz duː juː ˈhæv? ˈdʒʌst ˈfɑː?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Yes, just Fah. She's in high school now.
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs, ˈdʒʌst ˈfɑː. ʃiːz ɪn ˈhaɪ ˌskuːl ˈnaʊ.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Do you get along with her?
dialogue.reading: duː juː ˈɡɛt əˈlɔːŋ wɪð hɜːr?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Most of the time. But when I go home, she always borrows my clothes, and I have to put up with it!
dialogue.reading: ˈmoʊst əv ðə ˈtaɪm. bʌt wɛn aɪ ˈɡoʊ ˈhoʊm, ʃiː ˈɔːlweɪz ˈbɑːroʊz maɪ ˈkloʊðz, ənd aɪ ˈhæf tə ˈpʊt ˈʌp wɪð ɪt!

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Ha! My brother is the same. Older sisters always have to put up with something!
dialogue.reading: ˈhɑː! maɪ ˈbrʌðər ɪz ðə ˈseɪm. ˈoʊldər ˈsɪstərz ˈɔːlweɪz ˈhæf tə ˈpʊt ˈʌp wɪð ˈsʌmθɪŋ!

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: But she looks up to me. She wants to study English like me.
dialogue.reading: bʌt ʃiː ˈlʊks ˈʌp tə miː. ʃiː ˈwɑːnts tə ˈstʌdi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ laɪk miː.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: That's nice. Who do you look up to?
dialogue.reading: ðæts ˈnaɪs. ˈhuː duː juː ˈlʊk ˈʌp ˈtuː?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: My parents. They're teachers, and they work very hard.
dialogue.reading: maɪ ˈpɛrənts. ðɛr ˈtiːtʃərz, ənd ðeɪ ˈwɜːrk ˈvɛri ˈhɑːrd.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: I'd love to see them again. That dinner at your house was so good!
dialogue.reading: aɪd ˈlʌv tə ˈsiː ðɛm əˈɡɛn. ðæt ˈdɪnər ət jʊr ˈhaʊs wʌz ˈsoʊ ˈɡʊd!

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Come home with me next weekend. You can catch up with Fah, too.
dialogue.reading: ˈkʌm ˈhoʊm wɪð miː ˈnɛkst ˈwiːkɛnd. juː kən ˈkætʃ ˈʌp wɪð ˈfɑː, ˈtuː.
